paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Paul stands in front of a governor with a clear conscience and a hope in God, and that hope is the resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked (Acts 24:15, 16). His accusers brought flattery and big charges. Paul brought the truth and nothing to hide.

Now look at Felix. He was "well informed about the Way" (Acts 24:22). Then he heard Paul talk about righteousness, self-control and the coming judgment, and he "became frightened" and said, "When I find the time, I will call for you" (Acts 24:25). Felix kept sending for Paul, but he was hoping for a bribe, and two years later Paul was still in prison (Acts 24:26, 27).

So here's the lesson, baker. Knowing about God is not the same as answering Him. Felix had the information and the invitation, and he kept hitting snooze on both. Don't wait for a better time to listen, and let the Word change you today, like Paul, who strived to keep a clear conscience before God and man (Acts 24:16).
